risks.title: PA oscillation or spurious output above simulation at 146 MHz

statement.condition: the 5 W PA (TX) is verified before fabrication only by LTspice simulation with vendor or fitted device models whose accuracy at 144 to 148 MHz and 5 W output has not been confirmed by measurement, the owner's bench has no oscilloscope (SI-013), and the tinySA Ultra spectrum analyzer the owner committed to buy (SI-034) is not yet in hand or characterized (SI-003, SI-010)
statement.departure: the built PA oscillating, or producing harmonic and spurious levels higher than simulated
statement.asset: the TX subsystem (PA stage and output low-pass filter) and the 47 CFR 97.307 emission requirements allocated to it
statement.consequence: first-power-on failure of the transmitter, a second board spin (USD 300 to 800, 6 to 12 weeks), and a possible emission-limit exceedance that the bench cannot detect until the analyzer and its attenuator are characterized (RSK-011)

risks.likelihood_rationale: Single simulation chain (LTspice) with device models not validated against measured data at VHF and no prototype stage before the turnkey build. Anchor level 3: an analysis will exist but model fidelity is unconfirmed.
risks.consequence_rationale: Driving dimensions first_power_on, cost, schedule, performance_margin and safety all at 4: an unstable PA means the core TX function does not work and a second fabrication plus assembly run is needed; a spurious level above the 97.307(e) limit is a regulatory requirement miss (regulatory rule of process section 7); harmful interference to a safety-of-life or other service is the Critical severity of HZ-008, which maps to register safety 4 (hazard link rule, process section 1). PA self-heating itself is bounded by the supply current limit and the thermal response of the safety manager (RSK-006). An output-power shortfall of a stable PA is RSK-027.
risks.source: Formulation risk identification 2026-09-25 against SI-003, SI-010, SI-013; condition updated the same day for SI-034

steps.action: Select an RF power device that satisfies the sourcing constraint of SI-028 (ADR-012), has a vendor SPICE or S-parameter model and a vendor reference design or evaluation board covering 2 m; record the choice in a trade study (single-source and critical part, process section 14.1 (b)).

Run a small-signal stability analysis (Rollett K and mu factors) of the PA from 1 MHz to 1 GHz in LTspice with results exported and checked by a Python pass/fail script; require K > 1.2 and mu > 1.1 at every frequency with nominal, +10 % and -10 % passive tolerances.
steps.artifact: docs/design/analysis/pa-stability.md plus the deck and checker under hardware/sim/pa/

steps.action: Run a transient FFT of the PA plus output filter at 5 W and show every harmonic and spurious product at least 10 dB below the 97.307(e) limit recorded in the TX regulatory requirement; feed the margin into TPM-007.

Add design-for-debug provisions: PA supply through a jumper with a current-sense point, bias set by a resistor with alternates listed in the BOM, output pi-network with alternate values, so the PA can be recovered by BOM alternates or vendor rework without a respin.
steps.artifact: docs/design/build-to-specification.md (design-for-debug section); hardware/kicad/ TX sheet; hardware/bom/ alternates column

steps.action: Validate the LTspice toolchain (SWE-136) against a published VHF amplifier reference design and record the comparison of gain and stability.

Bench bring-up: measure the PA input and output matching networks with the NanoVNA before PA enable; enable the PA at reduced supply voltage first; observe the spectrum on the tinySA Ultra through the characterized attenuator (RSK-011 S2) before full power.

risks.title: LO frequency error exceeds the 500 Hz CW filter half-bandwidth

statement.condition: the receiver selectivity is a 500 Hz CW filter and the transmit and receive frequencies derive from a TCXO reference through the synthesizer chosen by cost and performance trade (SI-029, ADR-013); a typical +/-2.5 ppm TCXO alone corresponds to +/-365 Hz at 146 MHz before aging and temperature drift, and each of two cwht units (SI-019) carries its own error
statement.departure: the net frequency offset between two cwht units, or between a cwht and another station, exceeding the filter half-bandwidth of 250 Hz
statement.asset: the RX subsystem (CW filter and LO) and the stakeholder expectation of tuning to a frequency and chatting (SI-005)
statement.consequence: the other station's signal falling outside the passband, inaudible or badly detuned, so that operators cannot find each other without a search procedure

risks.likelihood_rationale: A +/-2.5 ppm reference alone consumes more than the filter half-bandwidth; without a tighter reference, receiver incremental tuning or a wider filter the departure is likely. Anchor level 4: no frequency error budget exists yet.
risks.consequence_rationale: Driving dimension performance_margin 4: the stakeholder expectation SI-005 (tune and chat) is not met as stated, although contacts remain possible by searching, so the MOE is degraded rather than lost. first_power_on 3: the radio works but a core use case is degraded until a firmware or filter change. Cost 2: a tighter TCXO grade is a USD 25 to 100 BOM delta over the build quantity.
risks.source: Formulation risk identification 2026-09-25 against SI-004, SI-005, SI-019

steps.action: Write the frequency error budget: TCXO initial tolerance, aging per year, temperature coefficient over 0 to 40 C, synthesizer resolution, filter center-frequency tolerance; state the worst-case two-unit offset and the offset after a single-point calibration.

Trade study of reference grade (0.5 ppm versus 2.5 ppm TCXO), filter bandwidth (500 Hz fixed versus 500 Hz and 1 kHz selectable) and receiver incremental tuning, scored with the register scales (process section 13).

Derive SW requirements for receiver incremental tuning, a tuning step of 50 Hz or finer, and a stored frequency calibration constant settable from the menu (frequency control is mission-critical per charter section 10).
Write the calibration procedure for the operations handbook: zero-beat against a signal of known frequency (a local repeater output or an already calibrated unit) and store the constant.
Analyze the CW filter center-frequency tolerance with a Monte Carlo over component tolerances and include it in the budget.

triggers.condition: Frequency budget worst-case error after calibration exceeds 100 Hz (40 % of the filter half-bandwidth)
triggers.response: Claude changes the TCXO grade or widens the filter and re-runs the budget before CDR; a CR is opened if a baselined requirement changes

triggers.condition: The selected TCXO has no distributor stock at PDR
triggers.response: Apply the RSK-005 alternate-part procedure the same session

mitigation.fallback: Widen the CW filter to 1 kHz nominal (CR against the selectivity requirement) and rely on receiver incremental tuning; contacts remain possible with reduced propagation advantage (SI-004).

risks.closure_criteria: Frequency accuracy requirement verified on two delivered units by a zero-beat test with a measured offset of 100 Hz or less after calibration.

statement.condition: Emulation is the optional, secondary pre-power-on evidence class for whole-binary scenarios (event ordering only, never timing; charter section 9, SI-026, ADR-011), implemented on rp2350-emu, a personal research project with no maintenance commitment (07 section 12), and no per-peripheral accreditation against the Pico 2 development board has been performed yet

statement.consequence: a firmware ordering fault discovered only on the assembled board, unit damage if the fault is in PA enable or charging sequencing, and loss of the Emulation evidence class for the affected requirements

risks.likelihood_rationale: rp2350-emu models a subset of peripherals and has no accreditation record; PIO and precise timer behavior are the least likely to be faithful, and a boot failure of a bare-metal rustos image is plausible. Anchor level 4: no fidelity assessment exists.

risks.title: PA junction temperature exceeds the device rating at 5 W

statement.condition: the PA dissipates on the order of 4 to 7 W of heat at 5 W RF output (40 to 55 % efficiency) inside a pocket-sized aluminum enclosure designed in OpenSCAD and CNC-machined by PCBWay (SI-001, SI-008, ADR-008); heat must flow from the device thermal pad through PCB vias and a mechanical interface to the enclosure wall, and no thermal instrument beyond a multimeter thermocouple is available (SI-013)
statement.departure: the PA junction temperature exceeding the device rating during sustained CW keying
statement.asset: the TX subsystem (PA device) and the sustained 5 W operating scenario
statement.consequence: PA derating or thermal shutdown during contacts, and shortened device life or failure of the PA

risks.likelihood_rationale: Several watts in a pocket enclosure is a tight thermal design; no thermal budget exists yet and the PCB-to-enclosure interface is undefined. Anchor level 3.
risks.consequence_rationale: Driving dimension performance_margin 4: sustained 5 W output (SI-003, a key driving expectation) is not met if the PA must fold back. Safety 4: an overheated device is a cause of HZ-003, which docs/safety/hazards.json 0.2.0-pha rates Critical (register safety 4, the hazard link rule minimum of 06 section 1); the device can be destroyed without fire and the heated enclosure can burn the operator. Cost and schedule 3: an enclosure or interface redesign and a new CNC part. The hand-hold surface temperature is RSK-026.
risks.source: Formulation risk identification 2026-09-25 against SI-001, SI-003, SI-008

steps.action: Thermal budget: dissipation at an assumed 50 % CW key-down duty cycle and a 5 min continuous key-down worst case; thermal resistance chain junction-to-case, pad-to-PCB, PCB-to-enclosure, enclosure-to-ambient; predicted junction temperature at 25 C and 40 C ambient (the surface prediction is RSK-026 S1 in the same budget).

Design the thermal interface (standoff or gap pad from the PCB thermal area to the enclosure wall) in the OpenSCAD model, render and inspect it (charter section 11 rule 3), and fit-check it with an H2C printed mock-up (SI-012).

NTC thermistor at the PA and firmware thermal foldback and shutdown as a safety-critical function (SW-SAFE thermal monitor with SW-TXSEQ actuation, 07 section 14.1; charter section 10, SWE-134 provisions); derive the SW requirements.
Bench verification: 5 min key-down into the dummy load inside the enclosure while logging the NTC over serial.

triggers.condition: Thermal budget predicts junction temperature above 80 % of the rated maximum at 25 C ambient and 5 min key-down
triggers.response: Claude redesigns the interface or proposes reduced power by CR; the item is a PDR lien until resolved

triggers.condition: Bench NTC reading rises more than 15 C above the budget prediction
triggers.response: Owner stops the test; Claude opens an NCR and revisits the budget

mitigation.fallback: Firmware limits key-down duty cycle or reduces PA drive when hot; the owner accepts reduced sustained power through a CR.

risks.closure_criteria: PA thermal requirement verified on the delivered unit at SAR with the 5 min key-down test inside the enclosure and the NTC log within the budget.

risks.title: Headphone output limiting fails to bound the sound level

statement.condition: receive audio and sidetone are delivered to headphones of 16 to 64 ohm with sensitivities up to about 122 dB per volt; an unrestricted headphone amplifier of the class under consideration can produce 113 to 126 dB SPL and a firmware fault can output a full-scale tone or a click at key-down or power-on (HZ-005); audio output limiting is a safety-critical software function (charter section 10), and the hardware ceiling network and the limiter are proposed controls, not yet designed
statement.departure: the hardware output ceiling or the sample-domain limiter failing to bound the headphone level, or a full-scale tone or click reaching the headphones at key-down, power-on or on a firmware fault
statement.asset: the operator's hearing (HZ-005), the RX audio chain and the sidetone
statement.consequence: acoustic shock or a hearing threshold shift for the operator

risks.likelihood_rationale: The controls are defined in the hazard analysis and are conventional (passive ceiling, limiter, mute ramp, enable sequencing), but no level budget exists and the earbud sensitivity spread is wide. Anchor level 3.
risks.consequence_rationale: Driving dimension safety 4: HZ-005 (hearing damage) is Critical, which maps to register safety 4. first_power_on 3: a passive network change is an 0402 rework the owner cannot do, so the audio subsystem is degraded until vendor rework. performance_margin 3: the headphone level-cap requirement (MOP-013) is not met. A capped sidetone that is too quiet is a plan trigger, not this departure.

statement.condition: keying drives PA enable and is a safety-critical software function (charter section 10; SW-KEYER, SW-TXSEQ and SW-SAFE in 07 section 14.1); one 3.5 mm TRS key jack accepts straight keys, paddles and mono plugs (SI-018, SI-034, ADR-009); HZ-004 names the causes (a closed or stuck contact at power-on or during operation, a mono plug read as a closed ring, a firmware or reset fault) and HZ-010 adds RF pickup on key leads about half a wavelength long at 146 MHz; their controls, including an independent hardware PA-enable cutoff of 7.5 to 13 s (HZ-004 K5), are proposed and not yet designed or verified

statement.asset: the TX PA enable path (SW-KEYER, SW-TXSEQ, SW-SAFE and the hardware cutoff), the operator and bystanders (HZ-004, HZ-010) and the licensee's Part 97 compliance
statement.consequence: an unintended carrier that heats the PA and exposes bystanders until a time-out acts, interference to other stations, and a firmware or key-input rework

risks.title: Antenna port retention fails under the whip side load

statement.condition: the SMA antenna jack on the end of a pocket radio sees 2 to 4 N.m from a 5 to 10 N side load on a 0.40 m whip (HZ-009); the enclosure is CNC-machined 6061 aluminum from an OpenSCAD model (SI-008, SI-032, ADR-008); HZ-009 K1 and K2 require the jack retained by the enclosure boss, not the PCB, and a 4.0 N.m port rating; no load analysis exists yet; the owner can fit-check with H2C prints (SI-012) but cannot re-machine anodized aluminum or rework the PCB (SI-011)
statement.departure: the antenna boss or jack retention failing, or the jack transferring the whip load into the PCB, under the whip side load
statement.asset: the antenna port, the PCB at the connector and the TX output path (HZ-009)
statement.consequence: a broken antenna port with PCB damage that the owner cannot repair, the radio inoperative, and a second CNC order or a spare board (USD 100 to 800, 3 to 12 weeks)

risks.likelihood_rationale: Pocket carry (SI-001) makes side loads routine and no load analysis exists; the fit-check print catches geometry but not material strength. Anchor level 3.
risks.consequence_rationale: Driving dimension first_power_on 4: PCB damage at the connector stops the TX function and the owner cannot rework it. Safety 3: HZ-009 is Marginal (register safety 3). Cost and schedule 3: a second CNC order or a spare board population.
risks.source: Split from RSK-018 on 2026-09-25 after independent review (process section 4: antenna-port retention and sharp edges harm different assets and have different driving dimensions); hazard link rule (process section 1) for HZ-009; ConOps section 8 candidate ANT-R1 (docs/research/antenna-and-erp.md) merged 2026-09-25

steps.action: Antenna port load analysis: 4.0 N.m static bending moment in any direction, jack retained by the enclosure boss and not by the PCB, PCB strain relief at the connector (HZ-009 K1, K2; moved from RSK-018 S2).
H2C fit-check of the boss, jack and nut with the real PCB and a static load test of 10 N at 0.40 m on the printed part before the CNC order (HZ-009 K6).
Derive the ME requirements from the HZ-009 controls (port moment, boss retention, 500 mating cycles at the specified coupling torque).
Receipt inspection of the CNC part: jack retention and a bending check at reduced load, boss dimensions against the drawing.
Handbook: finger-tight only, never a wrench; remove the antenna for pocket carry; telescopic antennas only with the radio set down (HZ-009 K5).

triggers.condition: The owner flags a loose jack or boss deflection on a fit-check print
triggers.response: Claude changes the model before the CNC order; an open item is a CDR lien

triggers.condition: A PCBWay CNC DFM comment changes the boss or the wall thickness
triggers.response: Claude opens a CR if the product baseline changes (05 section 5) and re-runs S1

triggers.condition: Receipt inspection finds a jack that moves under load
triggers.response: Claude opens an NCR; the owner decides between a printed boss collar and a second CNC order

mitigation.fallback: A printed (H2C) antenna-boss collar until a second CNC order, and a flexible whip only (HZ-009 K5); CR to the ME requirements.

risks.closure_criteria: Antenna port load analysis approved at CDR, the receipt-inspection bending check passed, and the ME requirements derived from HZ-009 verified at SAR.

risks.title: Enclosure hand-hold surface exceeds 48 C during sustained keying

statement.condition: the aluminum enclosure is the PA heatsink (ADR-008) and the PA dissipates on the order of 4 to 7 W at 5 W output; HZ-003 K1 sets the hand-hold surface limit at 48 C for 5 min of continuous key-down at 5 W and 25 C ambient (a project proposal, hazard analysis open item 7); no thermal budget exists yet and the only thermal instrument is the multimeter thermocouple (SI-013)
statement.departure: the enclosure hand-hold surface exceeding 48 C during sustained CW keying at 5 W
statement.asset: the operator's hand (HZ-003) and the ME enclosure
statement.consequence: a contact burn at the hand-hold surface, up to a burn needing medical treatment (HZ-003, Critical), that forces the operator to set the radio down, and a thermal-interface or enclosure redesign with a second CNC order

risks.likelihood_rationale: Several watts spread over a pocket-sized aluminum shell is close to the touch limit and no budget exists yet. Anchor level 3.
risks.consequence_rationale: Driving dimension safety 4: docs/safety/hazards.json 0.2.0-pha rates HZ-003 Critical (a burn needing medical treatment; register safety 4, the hazard link rule minimum of 06 section 1). Cost and schedule 3: a redesign needs a new CNC part at USD 100 to 300 and 3 to 6 weeks. first_power_on 1: the board works.
risks.source: Split from RSK-006 on 2026-09-25 after independent review (process section 4: the surface burn harms a different asset than the junction over-temperature); hazard link rule (process section 1) for HZ-003

steps.action: Surface-temperature prediction in the thermal budget at 25 C and 40 C ambient for 5 min of continuous key-down at 5 W and for the 1:9 duty cycle (HZ-003 K1, K7).
Derive the ME surface-temperature requirement and the handbook statement on continuous key-down and transmitting from a pocket (HZ-003 K1, K6).
Bench: enclosure surface temperature at the hand-hold areas with the multimeter thermocouple during the 5 min key-down case.

triggers.condition: The thermal budget predicts the hand-hold surface above 48 C at 25 C ambient and 5 min key-down
triggers.response: Claude redesigns the thermal path or proposes a key-down limit by CR before CDR; the item is a PDR lien until resolved

triggers.condition: A Bench surface reading exceeds 48 C
triggers.response: Owner stops the test; Claude opens an NCR and revisits the budget

mitigation.fallback: A firmware key-down duty limit or thermal fold-back (RSK-006 S3) keeps the surface below 48 C, accepted by the owner through a CR with the handbook warning, or an insulating grip sleeve printed on the H2C (SI-012).

risks.closure_criteria: Surface-temperature requirement verified on the delivered unit at SAR with the 5 min key-down case inside the enclosure.

risks.title: PA output power below the 5 W requirement

statement.condition: the 5 W carrier output (SI-003, ADR-003) is predicted before fabrication only by LTspice with device models unconfirmed at 144 to 148 MHz; the PA device is constrained to parts sourced from DigiKey, Mouser or PCBWay's turnkey distributors (SI-028, ADR-012) and is not selected yet; efficiency at the 5 W step is TPM-004 and output power accuracy at each step is TPM-015
statement.departure: the built PA delivering less than 5 W at the antenna port at the nominal pack voltage with the ALC at the top step
statement.asset: the TX subsystem (PA stage, matching and output low-pass filter) and the 5 W stakeholder expectation SI-003
statement.consequence: a key driving expectation missed (for example 4 W instead of 5 W), a CR against the output-power requirement, or a PA rework or respin to restore it

risks.likelihood_rationale: A single simulation chain with unvalidated VHF device models and no prototype stage; output power is sensitive to matching and device spread. Anchor level 3.
risks.consequence_rationale: Driving dimension performance_margin 4: SI-003 (5 W) is a stakeholder input. first_power_on, cost and schedule 3: the radio still transmits, and restoring power needs BOM alternates or vendor rework (USD 100 to 300, 3 to 6 weeks).
risks.source: Split from RSK-001 on 2026-09-25 after independent review (process section 4: the output-power shortfall is a non-safety departure and cannot share the HZ-008 safety family)

steps.action: Score output power at 5 W and 7.4 V pack voltage with at least 1 dB margin in the PA-device trade study (process section 14.1 (b); shared with RSK-001 S1).

Power budget: LTspice large-signal simulation of PA, matching and output filter at 6.4, 7.4 and 8.4 V pack voltage with component tolerances; output at the antenna port at least 1 dB above 5 W at 6.4 V.
Design-for-debug alternates for the matching network and bias so that output can be restored by BOM alternates or vendor rework (shared with RSK-001 S4).
Bench: output power at each step into the dummy load with the RF probe and the tinySA Ultra through the characterized attenuator (04 section 6.2).

triggers.condition: Simulated output at 6.4 V pack voltage is below 5.6 W (1 dB margin) at CDR
triggers.response: Claude changes the matching network or the PA device before CDR; a CR is opened if the output-power requirement must change

triggers.condition: Measured output is below 5 W at the top step at TRR
triggers.response: Claude opens an NCR and evaluates BOM alternates; the owner decides between rework and a CR to the requirement

mitigation.fallback: Operate at the achieved power through a CR to the 5 W requirement accepted by the owner; otherwise a PA rework or respin funded from the cost-estimate contingency (RSK-008).

risks.closure_criteria: TX output-power requirement verified by Test on the delivered unit at every power step, with no NCR open against output power.

risks.title: Unlicensed person transmits on a loaned or unattended unit

statement.condition: units are loaned to licensed friends (SI-019, SI-030, ADR-014) and may be handed around at gatherings; ADR-015 (proposed, owner decision at SRR) makes each licensee the station licensee and control operator of the unit held (OPS-A) and adds a licensee-settable receive-only guest lock (FW-03) that is not yet a requirement; an unlicensed person may key only as a supervised third party (docs/research/regulatory-corpus-and-operators.md F4)
statement.departure: an unlicensed person keying a cwht unit with no licensed control operator at that unit
statement.asset: the licensee's compliance with 47 CFR 97.5 and 97.103 (SI-014) and the owner's standing in the local amateur community
statement.consequence: an unlawful transmission, FCC enforcement exposure for the station licensee, and community harm

risks.likelihood_rationale: The research report rates the likelihood moderate in the 'play radio' use case (SI-019); the guest lock that removes the main pathway is proposed but not yet a requirement. Anchor level 3.
risks.consequence_rationale: Driving dimension performance_margin 4: a 47 CFR Part 97 requirement is not met (consequence scale, performance column). The other dimensions do not apply.
risks.source: ConOps section 8 candidate REG-4 (docs/research/regulatory-corpus-and-operators.md, Risks); hazard analysis section 12 HZ-006 row (unlicensed operation); entered 2026-09-25

steps.action: Guest-lock requirement: a licensee-settable receive-only mode in which key events produce no PA enable, persisted across power cycles, with HostUnit and Bench cases (ADR-015 FW-03).
Owner decision on ADR-015 at SRR recorded in the decision memo.
Operator rules card and the handbook operator model (OPS-A, OPS-C; DOC-02).

triggers.response: Claude re-assesses this risk the same session and proposes an alternative control to the owner (loaned units shipped with the guest lock on)

triggers.condition: A friend reports an unlicensed transmission on a loaned unit
triggers.response: Owner recalls the unit; Claude opens an NCR against the operator model and re-assesses this risk

mitigation.fallback: Loaned units ship with the guest lock enabled and no call sign stored, so that transmitting needs the licensee's own setup action; CR to the SW requirements.

risks.title: SAR by analogy understates the actual SAR of cwht

statement.condition: the portable-posture SAR evidence is SAR by analogy at the high database value of certified VHF handhelds, 0.35 W/kg per W at 1 g (docs/research/rf-exposure-evaluation.md, proposed decision RFX-D6); FCC acceptance of analogy is conditioned on a strong similarity to a database radio, which cwht's aluminum enclosure, end-mounted whip and different antenna weaken, and the database spread is 7:1; at 5 W continuous CW the licensee tier keeps 5.7x margin at the high value (HZ-001)
statement.departure: the actual peak spatial-average SAR of cwht in the portable posture exceeding the high analogy value
statement.asset: the operating licensee (HZ-001) and the RF Exposure Evaluation
statement.consequence: a smaller licensee-tier margin than evaluated (the occupational limit is still met below about 5.7 times the analogy value) and a revised evaluation

risks.likelihood_rationale: The high database value already sits at the top of a 7:1 spread of certified radios; exceeding it needs cwht to be worse than every database radio. Anchor level 2: analysis with more than 2x margin.
risks.consequence_rationale: Driving dimensions safety, schedule and performance_margin at 2: exposure stays within the FCC limit with less than 2x margin in the worst credible case (safety 2, HZ-001 Marginal); a revised evaluation costs 1 to 3 weeks. The general-population case is RSK-016.
risks.source: ConOps section 8 candidate RFX-R1 (docs/research/rf-exposure-evaluation.md); hazard analysis section 12 HZ-001 row (a risk for SAR analogy validity, safety 2, accepted after RFX-D6); entered 2026-09-25

steps.action: Owner decision RFX-D6 on accepting SAR by analogy at the high database value, recorded with the RF Exposure Evaluation approval at PDR; on approval this risk moves to Accepted with the licensee-tier margin as rationale.
Reference antenna not shorter than the evaluated whip, because a shorter whip raises local SAR (RFX-11, RFX-15).

triggers.condition: A primary SAR dataset or KDB 447498 obtained by the owner (hazard analysis open item 9) shows a VHF handheld above 0.35 W/kg per W
triggers.response: Claude revises the evaluation with the new high value and re-assesses this risk and RSK-016 the same session

triggers.condition: The reference antenna changes to a shorter whip
triggers.response: Claude re-assesses this risk before the change is approved

mitigation.fallback: Lower the default power step in the hand-held posture by CR, or add a numerical SAR estimate (open-source FDTD with a simple phantom, docs/research/part97-regulatory-basis.md REG-1).

risks.closure_criteria: Accepted by the owner under RFX-D6 with the licensee-tier margin as rationale, or the analogy superseded by a measurement or numerical estimate that shows the margin.

risks.title: PA damaged by a detuned or mismatched antenna

statement.condition: operators attach the antennas they own to the SMA port, including detuned, broken or counterfeit whips (docs/research/antenna-and-erp.md F6, F12); HZ-003 K5 and HZ-009 K3 propose a PA device with load ruggedness of at least 20:1 VSWR at rated power and survival of 60 s of key-down into any load up to 10:1 and into open and short circuits (ANT-04), with an optional forward and reverse power detector; the PA device is not selected yet (RSK-001 S1)
statement.departure: the PA device failing or degrading when keyed into a load with SWR above 3:1, an open or a short
statement.asset: the TX PA and the operating scenario of friends using their own antennas (SI-019)
statement.consequence: a unit that no longer transmits, a PA replacement the owner cannot hand-solder (vendor rework), and loss of the unit for weeks

risks.likelihood_rationale: The research report rates the likelihood Medium; mismatch tolerance depends on a device not yet selected. Anchor level 3.
risks.consequence_rationale: Driving dimensions first_power_on, cost, schedule and performance_margin at 3: the TX subsystem is lost until a vendor rework (USD 100 to 300, 3 to 6 weeks), and the load-tolerance requirement (ANT-04) is a Baseline requirement.
risks.source: ConOps section 8 candidate ANT-R2 (docs/research/antenna-and-erp.md); entered 2026-09-25

steps.action: Make load ruggedness of at least 20:1 VSWR at rated power a mandatory criterion of the PA-device trade study (RSK-001 S1, HZ-003 K5).
Derive the load-tolerance requirement (60 s into any load up to 10:1, open and short; ANT-04) and decide the forward and reverse power detector with fold-back above 3:1 by ADR.
Bench: 60 s of key-down into open, short and a 10:1 mismatch, first at reduced power and then at 5 W, with output re-measured into the dummy load afterwards.
Handbook SWR screen with the NanoVNA before the first use of an unknown antenna (ANT-05).

triggers.response: Claude proposes the detector with fold-back as a required control by ADR before PDR closes

triggers.response: Owner stops the test; Claude opens an NCR

mitigation.fallback: Add the SWR detector and firmware fold-back by CR, and restrict delivered units to the reference antenna in the handbook until then.

risks.title: PWM audio noise masks weak CW signals

statement.condition: receive audio and sidetone are generated by RP2350 PWM sharing supply and ground with the digital section; display SPI, flash and synthesizer activity can couple into the audio as hiss or ticks (docs/research/audio-output-and-hearing-safety.md F1); the owner has no oscilloscope (SI-013), so PWM noise can only be judged by listening and with the multimeter on the first board; a PCM5102A DAC footprint is kept unpopulated as a fallback (F31)
statement.departure: audible PWM hiss, ticks or digital interference in the headphones at a level that masks signals near the receiver's minimum discernible signal
statement.asset: the RX audio chain and the weak-signal CW operating scenario (SI-005)
statement.consequence: degraded weak-signal reception and population of the DAC footprint by vendor rework

risks.likelihood_rationale: Shared-supply PWM audio is prone to digital noise and the effect can only be judged on the first board. Anchor level 3.
risks.consequence_rationale: Driving dimensions first_power_on and performance_margin at 3: the audio subsystem is degraded until vendor rework populates the DAC, and the receiver MDS requirement (TPM-005) is degraded.
risks.source: ConOps section 8 candidate R-AUD-1 (docs/research/audio-output-and-hearing-safety.md); entered 2026-09-25

steps.action: DMA-fed PWM with a dedicated analog return and supply filtering; LTspice of the reconstruction filter and supply rejection; derive the SW-AUDIO DMA-PWM requirement.
Keep the unpopulated PCM5102A footprint and its BOM line in the release package (F31).
Bench listening test and MDS measurement with display, flash and synthesizer activity running (TPM-005).

triggers.condition: The bench listening test shows audible ticks or hiss above an MDS-level signal
triggers.response: Claude opens an NCR and the owner decides on populating the DAC footprint by vendor rework

triggers.condition: The dev-board check (RSK-012 S3) shows audible PWM artifacts in the sidetone
triggers.response: Claude revises the PWM scheme before CDR

mitigation.fallback: Populate the PCM5102A DAC footprint by vendor rework (F31) with a firmware build for the DAC path.

risks.closure_criteria: Receiver MDS and audio noise cases passed on the delivered unit with the selected audio path.

risks.title: Pico 2 USB power path overheats at the charging current

statement.condition: the pack charges through the Pico 2 module's micro-USB connector (SI-022, ADR-004), whose connector, D1 bypass and VBUS copper have no published current rating; HZ-011 K4 limits the input current to 500 mA by default, never above 1.5 A, and above 500 mA only after DCP or CDP identification or an explicit setting; charging above 500 mA through the module is unqualified (docs/research/power-tree-and-charging.md R-PWR-01)
statement.departure: the Pico 2 micro-USB connector, D1 bypass or VBUS copper overheating or failing at the configured charging current
statement.asset: the PWR charging path, the Pico 2 module and the operator handling the radio while it charges (HZ-011)
statement.consequence: a hot connector or module (minor burn), a damaged Pico 2 module that the owner must replace by hand, and a charging-current CR

risks.likelihood_rationale: No rating exists for the module path and the measurement is not done; the 500 mA default is conservative, but any higher budget is unqualified. Anchor level 3.
risks.consequence_rationale: Driving dimensions safety and performance_margin at 3: a hot connector can cause a first-aid burn (HZ-011 Marginal, register safety 3), and a permanent 500 mA cap may miss the charging-time requirement. first_power_on 2: the Pico 2 is a hand-soldered module the owner can replace.
risks.source: ConOps section 8 candidate R-PWR-01 (docs/research/power-tree-and-charging.md); hazard analysis section 12 HZ-011 row; entered 2026-09-25

steps.action: Derive the input-current limit requirements (500 mA default, 1.5 A ceiling, above 500 mA only after port identification; HZ-011 K4) and the firmware charging-current setting.

Measurement before any budget above 500 mA (REQ candidate PWR-USB-02): connector and module temperature with the multimeter thermocouple at 500 mA, 1 A and 1.5 A for 2 h on a dev-board Pico 2 (Bench, credit: false).

triggers.response: Claude proposes the second USB connector (rejected by SI-022 unless this test fails) to the owner before CDR

risks.title: Bench fire or treatable burn during owner hand assembly

statement.condition: the kit model has the owner hand-solder the through-hole parts and exposed-pad modules of up to five units (SI-031, SI-035, ADR-007, REQ-SYS-137, REQ-SYS-138); docs/safety/hazards.json 0.2.0-pha rates this activity HZ-015 Catastrophic-D (a bench fire from an iron left energized off its stand) with controls K1 (temperature-controlled station with stand, auto-sleep and earthed tip), K2 (fume extraction), K4 (hand-assembly procedure) and K5 (TRR safety line) still without requirements (OQ-SAF-019), and the owner's bench gear list CON-016 records no soldering station
statement.departure: a bench fire, a burn needing medical treatment or an eye injury occurring while the owner hand-assembles or reworks a unit
statement.asset: the owner as test operator, the household and the property at the home bench (HZ-015)
statement.consequence: an uncontained bench fire or an injury needing medical treatment, and a halted assembly of the remaining units

risks.likelihood_rationale: HZ-015 rates the uncontrolled fire case D (Remote: not expected in the fleet life of at most five units but credible) and the treatable-burn case C; before the TRR horizon that is the 5 % to 20 % band of 06 section 6 (level 2, Unlikely). No design-analysis anchor applies to a procedure hazard, so the probability band decides and confidence is Low (the owner's iron is not recorded).
risks.consequence_rationale: Driving dimension safety 5: a fire not contained to the unit is Catastrophic on the docs/safety/hazards.json scale (register safety 5, the hazard link rule minimum for HZ-015). first_power_on 3: heat or ESD damage to a vendor-placed part (RP2350 module, PA, LNA, TCXO) found at first power-on degrades a subsystem and needs vendor rework or a spare population. Cost 2 and schedule 2: a replacement part and a re-solder session (USD 25 to 100, 1 to 3 weeks). performance_margin 1.
risks.source: Hazard link rule (06 section 1) for HZ-015, added in docs/safety/hazards.json 0.2.0-pha (hazard analysis OQ-SAF-020: no risk carried it); opened 2026-09-25 by the integrating session

steps.action: Write requirements for the HZ-015 controls K1, K2, K4 and K5 (station with stand, auto-sleep and earthed tip; fume extraction; hand-assembly procedure; TRR safety line and as-built entries), closing OQ-SAF-019; the hazard analysis author then sets their control_req_ids in hazards.json.

The owner confirms or obtains a temperature-controlled soldering station with a stand, an auto-sleep or auto-off timer and an earthed tip, and a fume extractor; Claude records model and features as a stakeholder input and in HZ-015 K1, which removes the zero-fault-tolerant fire case.

Write the hand-assembly procedure (alloy and tip temperature, dwell limits and order, cells removed and USB disconnected, eye protection, hygiene, ESD strap and mat) into the hardware release package and have it independently reviewed before the procurement release.
TRR safety line: the test configuration record confirms that the procedure was followed, and each unit's as-built record lists the station, the alloy and any rework (HZ-015 K5).

triggers.condition: At the S2 check before the CDR readiness declaration the owner's iron has no stand, no auto-sleep or no earthed tip, or no fume extraction is available
triggers.response: Claude re-assesses likelihood and confidence the same session and proposes the station purchase or an alternative control to the owner before the procurement release; the CDR decision memo records the choice

triggers.condition: Any fire or smoke, burn needing treatment, eye injury, or vendor-placed part damaged during hand assembly or rework
triggers.response: The owner stops assembly; Claude opens an NCR and re-assesses this risk and HZ-015 in the same session before assembly resumes

mitigation.fallback: The through-hole and exposed-pad parts are assembled by a third party (PCBWay through-hole assembly or a local service) through a CR that changes the SI-031 assembly split, which removes the owner's hand assembly.

risks.closure_criteria: HZ-015 controls K1, K2, K4 and K5 allocated to requirements and verified by Inspection (procedure reviewed, station and extractor recorded, TRR safety line and as-built records complete) before the first hand assembly; the risk closes when HZ-015 reaches Controls verified.

candidates.rationale: Entered with REG-5 and RFX-R3 as one failure-mode family: same asset (the cited regulatory basis), same driving dimension (performance margin), one plan (process section 4).

candidates.summary: Unlicensed operation of a unit by a guest
Currency of the five 47 CFR 2.106 allocation rows
candidates.rationale: Same event family as REG-3 (a cited regulatory text changes unnoticed); its check is RSK-029 S2 (DECISION-10 browser check).

candidates.summary: Interpretation of third-party keying by a guest
candidates.rationale: Not a scored departure: the design supports either reading (guest lock FW-03, ADR-015), so an interpretation that limits third-party keying changes only the OPS-C text and the handbook, consequence 1 in every dimension. Re-open if an interpretation would require a firmware or hardware change.

candidates.summary: SAR-by-analogy validity for a homebrew form factor
Continuous tune carrier within 20 cm of a non-licensee
candidates.rationale: The 0.5 W tune default and 10 s time-out are RSK-016 controls (S2, S4): same persons (HZ-006), same driving dimension (safety 4) and plan.

candidates.summary: RF-exposure guidance in flux (OET 65 Supplement B, SAR exemptions)
candidates.rationale: Same event family as REG-3 (cited guidance changes unnoticed); its re-check is RSK-029 S2 and the second RSK-029 trigger.

candidates.summary: Connector or PCB damage from the antenna moment
candidates.rationale: RSK-025 (split from RSK-018 the same day) is this departure and carries HZ-009.

candidates.summary: PA damage into a detuned or counterfeit antenna
Table-top posture loses about 10 dB without a counterpoise
candidates.rationale: A known property of the reference quarter-wave whip without a counterpoise, not an uncertain event: it is designed for by the counterpoise attachment point (HZ-009 K4) and the ConOps posture guidance (section 3.6), and its effect on range is verified through the contact-range MOE. Re-open as a risk if the PDR requirements drop the counterpoise attachment.

candidates.summary: RF on the headphone and key leads
candidates.rationale: False keyer input from RF on the key lead is a cause of RSK-024 (HZ-010 K4 and K6 in steps S2 and S4); the audio thump on the headphone lead is a click cause bounded by the RSK-017 limiter and fade controls.

candidates.summary: Mono plug or stuck contact causes continuous transmission at power-on
candidates.rationale: A cause of RSK-024 (HZ-004 C-causes and the K1, K2 controls in step S1).

candidates.summary: Friends' keys may use mono plugs
candidates.rationale: A cause of RSK-024; the plug check and KEY CLOSED message are step S5 (HZ-004 K10).

candidates.summary: Earbuds up to 5 dB louder than the EN 50332-2 model
candidates.rationale: Same departure as RSK-017 (the level not bounded for the most sensitive earbud); RSK-017 S1 includes the 5 dB excess in the worst-case SPL.

candidates.summary: Pico 2 module USB current path unrated above 500 mA
Memory LCD unreadable in the dark
candidates.rationale: Not an uncertain event: revision A has no display light by design (D-UI-02 recommendation 'none in build 1'; the bezel keeps a front-light option), stated as an accepted limitation in the ConOps and decided by the owner on D-UI-02. Re-open as a risk if the owner makes night operation a requirement.
